# Implementation Plan: Capture-First Instrumentation for the codex-exec Lens Hang (D-001)

<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"ralph-codex-exec-lens-hang-instrumentation"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-07. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/ralph-codex-exec-lens-hang-instrumentation/plan.md`.*

## Overview

The ralph `codex-exec` research/review lens, invoked from inside a Copilot ralph member on
Windows (codex 0.135), can wedge the whole pipeline: codex spawns, produces no captured output,
never exits, orphans `codex.exe`, and the ~300s harness tool-timeout fails to reap it (observed
3× on 2026-06-07). This plan implements **D-001 (capture-first)**: port the proven Windows-safe
child-lifecycle machinery from the sibling `src/copilot-exec.mjs` into `src/codex-exec.mjs`, and
extend it so BOTH the child's stdout and stderr are drained/captured to per-lens sidecar files
(fd-backed — no inherited, undrained pipe), with a `RUST_LOG` phase trace, a bounded wrapper
timeout, a pre-kill process-tree + TCP-connection snapshot, and a `taskkill /T /F` subtree kill
so no `codex.exe` is orphaned.

It is **diagnosis + fix in one change**. The PRIMARY hypothesis is **pipe-buffer deadlock**:
`codex-exec.mjs` spawns with `stdio: ["pipe", "inherit", "inherit"]`, so neither stdout nor
stderr is drained by the wrapper — both are inherited up to the Copilot member harness. If that
consumer holds them as pipes and waits on process exit instead of draining continuously, the
Windows ~64KB OS pipe buffer fills and `codex.exe` blocks on `write()` forever (which also
explains the "no output captured" symptom). Switching to fd-backed sidecar files applies **no
write-backpressure**, so it eliminates the pipe-deadlock failure mode entirely. The MCP-block
hypothesis was **refuted** by the brainstorm's live repro (`codex exec` exit 0 in ~27s).

The decisive validation (Story US-001) runs the exact failing large/`xhigh` workload under BOTH
the current `inherit` stdio and the new fd-backed stdio, at low/no `RUST_LOG`: **if draining/
capturing the streams makes the hang vanish, that confirms the pipe-buffer deadlock was the root
cause.** If the hang persists under fd-backed capture, the sidecar's last log line decides
between `startup_remote_sync` and the `POST /responses` model stream (follow-up directions
D-002/D-003, out of scope here).

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context
- `src/codex-exec.mjs:80-84` — `spawn("codex", args, { env, shell: true, stdio: ["pipe","inherit","inherit"] })`.
  The wrapper writes the prompt to stdin then closes it; it never reads/drains the child's
  stdout or stderr. `waitForChild()` (203-227) blocks with no timeout, no signal handlers, no
  tree-kill. The header comment (line 8) says it "must not install signal handlers" and "Codex
  owns the output file directly through its own -o flag" — **this contract is the root cause**.
- `src/copilot-exec.mjs` already has the machinery to port: fd-backed stdout capture
  (`openSync(outputFile,"w")` → `stdio: ["ignore", outFd, "inherit"]`, 229-230/447-448, closed
  in `finally`), `killChildTree()` via `taskkill /T /F /PID` (107-128), and
  `registerCleanupHandlers()` for exit/SIGINT/SIGTERM with an `unregister()` contract (474-498).
  Note copilot-exec captures only stdout and still **inherits stderr** — the codex port must
  capture BOTH because codex's diagnostic trace goes to stderr.
- All callers are file-backed: `src/ralph.mjs` and `src/review-loop.mjs` pass `--output <file>`
  and read that FILE; the skills (`plan-with-ralph`, `review-changes`, `brainstorm-with-ralph`,
  `multi-model-investigate`, `agents/plan-reviewer.md`) write `--output <...>.txt` and read it.
  No caller consumes codex stdout as data; only live-terminal **visibility** uses the current
  `inherit` behavior.
- `src/review-loop.mjs:79` defaults `planningEngine: "codex"`, so a codex-exec hang wedges
  plan-fix iterations. (This plan's own Phase 4 review convergence was run with
  `--planning-engine copilot` for exactly this reason.)
- Live brainstorm evidence: a minimal `codex exec` (tiny prompt, stderr→file, `RUST_LOG=debug`)
  did NOT hang (exit 0, ~27s). `RUST_LOG=debug` phase markers seen: `thread/start`,
  `codex_core_plugins::manager: starting/completed remote plugin sync` (~10s network call even
  for 0 plugins), `model_client.stream_responses_api ... POST /responses`, and sub-second
  `SessionStart`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Stop` hooks.

### Technical Constraints
- **Exit-code contract must be preserved**: `child.exitCode`, else `128 + signalNum`, else `1`
  (codex-exec.mjs:203-227; AGENTS.md/CHANGELOG v5.45.0). A new bounded-timeout exit adds one
  distinct non-zero code (conventionally `124`).
- **Test surface pins the behavior to change**: `tests/test-codex-exec.mjs:120` asserts
  `stdio === ["pipe","inherit","inherit"]`; this must be updated to the fd-backed shape. Other
  cases (argv `-c` one element, `--output` present, exit-code preservation, output-file
  non-mutation) and `tests/test-regression-smoke-phase-3.mjs` + `tests/test-wrapper-rubric.sh`
  must stay green.
- `shell:true` is intentional (Windows `.cmd` shim resolution). It means `child.pid` is the
  cmd.exe wrapper, not `codex.exe`; `taskkill /T` on the spawned PID reaps the subtree, and the
  pre-kill snapshot must walk descendants (`Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` by `ParentProcessId`,
  recursively) plus `Get-NetTCPConnection -OwningProcess`.
- `RUST_LOG` must be merged into the spawn `env` WITHOUT mutating the caller's `process.env`;
  a caller-set `RUST_LOG` wins, else apply the default; the effective value is recorded in the
  sidecar header.
- `RUST_LOG=debug` changes timing (Heisenbug) — a low/no-log control mode is required so the
  A/B test does not alter the workload.
- Do not silently swallow failures: if `taskkill` or a snapshot command fails, record the
  failure in the sidecar rather than treating it as success.
- The snapshot is Windows-only and best-effort; guard the non-Windows path.

## Approach

### Architecture
Implement entirely inside `src/codex-exec.mjs::main()` around the current spawn block, porting
selected `copilot-exec.mjs` primitives and adapting them for **two** sidecar fds. No call-site
edits are required (sidecar dir defaults from `--output`), which keeps the conflict surface to a
single source file plus its tests and docs.

The child stdio changes from `["pipe", "inherit", "inherit"]` to **`["pipe", outFd, errFd]`**,
where `outFd`/`errFd` are `openSync(<sidecar>.out|.err, "w")` file descriptors. This is the
simplest correct concurrent drain: the OS writes each stream directly to its own file, so there
is **no Node-side single-threaded read-one-then-the-other risk and no pipe backpressure**.
Codex's `-o` result file is untouched (callers keep reading it). The wrapper gains a bounded
timeout, a pre-kill process-tree/TCP snapshot, a `killChildTree()`, and SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers
with an `unregister()` in `finally`.

### Implementation Strategy
The dangerous workload (the real large/`xhigh` hang) is deferred until AFTER the no-orphan safety
net exists, so the investigation never re-orphans `codex.exe`. US-001 proves the mechanism with a
**synthetic, deterministic** repro that cannot hang unboundedly; the **real-prompt** end-to-end
A/B confirmation runs in US-005, once US-004's `taskkill /T` reaping is in place.

1. **US-001** — Confirm/refute pipe-deadlock first with a SYNTHETIC, deterministic
   buffer-filling repro. Document the current no-drain wiring, then run a small harness that
   forces a child to write `> ~256KB` to an UNDRAINED inherited pipe (reproducing the Windows
   ~64KB-buffer block) vs the same child with stdout/stderr attached to FILES, each wrapped in an
   EXTERNAL watchdog (independent `Start-Process` timeout + `taskkill /T`) so no orphan can occur
   before US-004 lands. Record the inherit-vs-fd-backed outcome and attribution to a named,
   committed artifact (see Files to Create). This is the disconfirmation gate; it does NOT run the
   real flaky `xhigh` prompt.
2. **US-002** — Switch stdio to fd-backed dual sidecars (`.out` + `.err`), default
   `--sidecar-dir = dirname(--output)/lenses/`, names `codex-exec-<ts>.{out,err}`;
   `mkdirSync(sidecarDir, { recursive: true })` before opening fds; preserve `-o`; close fds in
   `finally`. This is the deadlock-eliminating fix.
3. **US-003** — Set `RUST_LOG` in the spawn env (codex-scoped default, caller override respected,
   no `process.env` mutation) so `.err` carries the named phase markers; add a low/no-log control
   flag/env; record the effective value in the sidecar header.
4. **US-004** — Add a bounded wrapper timeout + pre-kill snapshot (the spawned-PID process subtree
   + `Get-NetTCPConnection -OwningProcess`) written to a snapshot sidecar (recording any snapshot
   failure), then `killChildTree()` (`taskkill /T /F /PID`), recording the kill; add SIGINT/SIGTERM
   handlers (port) so an outer kill also reaps the subtree. Settle with a distinct timeout exit
   code.
5. **US-005** — The real-prompt end-to-end A/B confirmation (the exact failing large/`xhigh`
   prompt under both `inherit` and fd-backed stdio, low/no `RUST_LOG`), now safe because US-004's
   tree-kill prevents orphans; update/extend tests (stdio assertion, sidecar creation incl. the
   missing-`lenses/`-dir case, `-o` argv unchanged, timeout→tree-kill→no-orphan via injected
   hooks, signal cleanup); verify regression parity; revise the codex-exec header contract
   comment; update AGENTS.md + CHANGELOG; bump the 5 version stamps.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Change `codex-exec.mjs` child stdio so stdout AND stderr are captured to per-lens sidecar
  files instead of inherited; preserve codex's `-o` result file.
- Set `RUST_LOG` for lens runs (codex-scoped default; caller override respected) with a low/no-log
  control; record the effective value in the sidecar.
- Add a bounded wrapper timeout, `killChildTree()` (`taskkill /T /F /PID`), SIGINT/SIGTERM
  handlers, and a pre-kill process-tree + `Get-NetTCPConnection -OwningProcess` snapshot.
- An A/B reproduction recipe/harness (inherit vs fd-backed, low/no `RUST_LOG`) plus a recorded
  outcome that correctly attributes a vanished hang to pipe-deadlock (vs falsely crediting a fix
  for remote-sync / model-stream).
- Tests, regression parity, contract-comment revision, AGENTS.md/CHANGELOG, version stamps.

### Out of Scope
- Shipping a final root-cause fix for `startup_remote_sync` stalls or `POST /responses`
  model-stream stalls — those become follow-ups IF US-001 shows the hang persists under
  fd-backed capture (directions D-002/D-003).
- Changing `copilot-exec.mjs` (already has fd-capture + tree-kill).
- Any codex (Rust) source change. This is a Node wrapper / ralph-plugin change only.
- Disabling plugins/marketplace remote sync globally (D-002's mitigation, deferred).
- Editing call sites (the sidecar dir defaults from `--output`; the optional `--sidecar-dir`
  flag is available but no caller is required to pass it).

## Risk Areas
- **False root-cause confidence (carried from the devil's-advocate lens):** if the hang merely
  *vanishes* under fd-backed capture, attribute it to pipe-deadlock — do NOT claim remote-sync /
  model-stream are fixed. US-001's A/B (inherit vs fd-backed, low/no `RUST_LOG`) is mandatory.
- **Lost live visibility:** `inherit` currently streams codex's turn output to the parent
  terminal (and to `review-loop.mjs`/`ralph.mjs`'s live tailers). fd-backed capture moves it to
  the `.out` sidecar. Functional consumption (the `-o` file) is unaffected; live streaming of the
  raw child stream is lost by design. Callers' file tailers still show the `-o` result.
- **Tree-kill ancestry under `shell:true`:** the child PID is cmd.exe; verify `taskkill /T`
  reaches the `codex.exe` grandchild (it does — `/T` kills the subtree). The snapshot must
  descend recursively to enumerate `codex.exe`.
- **Timeout value selection:** the wrapper timeout must be < the caller's harness tool-timeout
  (~300s) so the wrapper self-reaps before the harness kills node (which is what orphans
  `codex.exe`). Make it configurable; pick a documented default below the harness bound.
- **`RUST_LOG=debug` Heisenbug:** default to a low/no-log mode; debug is opt-in.
- **Sidecar retention / disk:** verbose traces accumulate in job artifacts. Decide a retention
  policy (e.g. keep-on-failure, or last-N) — see Open Questions.
- **Test fakes:** the timeout/tree-kill test must inject `execFileSync`/timer hooks rather than
  invoking real `taskkill`; the existing `spawn` fake must be extended for fd + timer + kill.

## Acceptance Criteria
- After an induced wrapper timeout on a deliberately-long codex run, **no orphaned `codex.exe`**
  remains — verified by enumerating descendants of the spawned shell PID captured in the pre-kill
  snapshot (NOT a global `Get-Process codex`, which can false-fail on unrelated `codex.exe` from
  other sessions); the kill is recorded in the sidecar.
- Both a `.out` and an `.err` sidecar exist per codex-exec lens invocation and contain the
  child's stdout/stderr; codex's `-o` result file is still written on success; a missing
  `lenses/` directory is created (`mkdirSync(..., { recursive: true })`) rather than throwing.
- The `.err` sidecar contains `RUST_LOG` phase markers sufficient to distinguish startup-sync vs
  model-request vs hooks on a hang — concretely, at least the substrings `remote plugin sync`
  (startup-sync), `stream_responses_api` / `POST /responses` (model-request), and
  `SessionStart`/`Stop` (hooks); the effective `RUST_LOG` value is recorded in the sidecar header,
  and the default filter + env/flag precedence is documented (see US-003).
- **Synthetic A/B (US-001):** a deterministic buffer-filling repro (child writes `> ~256KB` to an
  undrained inherited pipe vs to files) is run under both stdio modes at low/no `RUST_LOG`, each
  under an external watchdog, and the outcome + attribution is recorded in
  `docs/codex-exec-hang-ab-findings.md` (inherited-pipe leg blocks ⇒ pipe-deadlock mechanism
  confirmed; fd-backed leg completes).
- **Real-prompt A/B (US-005):** the exact failing large/`xhigh` prompt is run under both current
  `inherit` stdio and the new fd-backed stdio (low/no `RUST_LOG`) — safe because US-004's
  tree-kill prevents orphans — and the outcome (hang vanishes ⇒ pipe-deadlock confirmed for the
  real workload; hang persists ⇒ last-log-line attributes the phase to remote-sync vs
  model-stream) is appended to the same findings note.
- No happy-path regression: a normal codex-exec lens still returns its result via `-o`, exits 0,
  and preserves the documented exit-code contract.
- `tests/test-codex-exec.mjs` updated and green; `tests/test-regression-smoke-phase-3.mjs`,
  `tests/test-wrapper-rubric.sh`, `tests/test-copilot-exec.mjs` green; AGENTS.md + CHANGELOG
  updated; the 5 version stamps bumped in lockstep.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

- **US-001 — Confirm/refute pipe-deadlock via a SYNTHETIC A/B repro harness (safe gate).**
  Document the current no-drain wiring; build a minimal harness that runs a deterministic
  buffer-filling child (writes `> ~256KB`) under (a) an undrained inherited pipe and (b)
  stdout/stderr attached to files, each wrapped in an EXTERNAL watchdog (`Start-Process` timeout +
  `taskkill /T`) so no orphan can occur before US-004 exists. Record the outcome + attribution to
  `docs/codex-exec-hang-ab-findings.md`. Does NOT run the real flaky `xhigh` prompt. Disconfirmation
  gate for the mechanism.
- **US-002 — Per-lens fd-backed capture of BOTH stdout and stderr.** Change the spawn stdio to
  `["pipe", outFd, errFd]` with `openSync` sidecars under `--sidecar-dir`
  (default `dirname(--output)/lenses/`, names `codex-exec-<ts>.{out,err}`);
  `mkdirSync(sidecarDir, { recursive: true })` before opening fds; close fds in `finally`;
  preserve `-o`. The deadlock-eliminating fix.
- **US-003 — `RUST_LOG` phase-trace tee + low/no-log control.** Merge a codex-scoped `RUST_LOG`
  default into the spawn env (caller-set `RUST_LOG` wins; no `process.env` mutation); record the
  effective value in the sidecar header; add a low/no-log control flag/env (Heisenbug guard).
  Pin the default filter and document precedence; the `.err` must surface the discriminating
  markers `remote plugin sync`, `stream_responses_api`/`POST /responses`, and `SessionStart`/`Stop`.
- **US-004 — Bounded wrapper timeout + pre-kill process-tree/TCP snapshot + tree-kill (no
  orphan).** Add a configurable timeout (`--timeout-ms`/env, documented default below the harness
  bound). On timeout and on SIGINT/SIGTERM: snapshot the spawned-shell-PID subtree (recursive
  `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` by `ParentProcessId`) + `Get-NetTCPConnection -OwningProcess` to a
  snapshot sidecar (recording any snapshot failure rather than swallowing it), then
  `killChildTree()` (`taskkill /T /F /PID`), record the kill, settle with a distinct timeout exit
  code; port `registerCleanupHandlers()` with `unregister()` in `finally`.
- **US-005 — Real-prompt A/B confirmation + tests, regression parity, contract revision, docs +
  version stamps.** Run the exact failing large/`xhigh` prompt under `inherit` vs fd-backed stdio
  (now safe via US-004's tree-kill) and append the result to the findings note. Update the stdio
  assertion; add sidecar/missing-dir/timeout/tree-kill/signal tests (injected hooks); verify
  regression-smoke + wrapper-rubric + copilot-exec stay green; scope the no-orphan assertion to
  spawned-PID descendants; revise the codex-exec header contract comment; add `## vX.Y.0 Behavioral
  Additions` to AGENTS.md + a CHANGELOG entry; bump the 5 version stamps.

## Suggested Decomposition

All stories edit the same single source file (`src/codex-exec.mjs`) and its co-located tests/docs.
There is no disjoint file footprint to exploit, and the test/doc/version-stamp story must land
last. Execute **serially as one cluster**.

### Cluster: codex-exec-capture-first
- Stories: [US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005]
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`src/codex-exec.mjs`, `tests/test-codex-exec.mjs`]; exclusive=[]; risk=high
- `execution_mode` rationale: Every story mutates `src/codex-exec.mjs` (and US-005 also touches
  the shared tests/docs/version stamps), so concurrent execution would produce guaranteed
  conflicts. Serialize.

## Open Questions
- **Wrapper timeout default value** — what exact default (and env/flag name) sits safely below
  every caller's harness tool-timeout (~300s) while not prematurely killing a legitimately long
  `xhigh` lens? (Recommendation: `CODEX_EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS`, default ~270000, overridable per call;
  finalize in US-004.)
- **Sidecar retention policy** — keep all `.out`/`.err`/snapshot sidecars, keep-on-failure only,
  or prune to last-N per job dir? Verbose `RUST_LOG` traces can be large. (Recommendation:
  keep-on-failure + a bounded last-N; finalize in US-002/US-004.)
- **Default `RUST_LOG` filter (recommendation, not a blocker)** — US-003 pins it; the recommended
  default is a codex-scoped filter that guarantees the discriminating markers
  (`remote plugin sync`, `stream_responses_api`/`POST /responses`, `SessionStart`/`Stop`) without
  flooding — e.g. `info` narrowed to `codex_core,codex_core_plugins,codex_*` — with a caller-set
  `RUST_LOG` taking precedence and a low/off control.
- **[INFERRED]** The impl targets the `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule (ralph-orchestration
  plugin). It requires a **submodule worktree** under
  `ai-developer-toolkit/.worktrees/<task-id>` and the **two-commit flow** (commit + push inside
